supersedes: dynamic-impact-v1 bounce artifact (trajectory split only; kept)

data.source: GAUGE public bouncing-ball trajectories (22 JSON files, 30 fps, mm)
data.split: selection = odd file IDs 1..21, held-out = even file IDs 2..22
data.observed_diversity: all 22 trials are repeats of one drop (release height 0.405-0.410 m, same xy); the held-out trajectory split therefore tests replicate transfer, not new conditions. The height axis below uses later apexes of the same real trajectories as lower-height re-releases.

fixed.initial_velocity: frame-0 start: zero (public-data limitation); apex re-release: central finite difference of frames k-1,k+1
fixed.sap_note: SAP ignores the shape 'restitution' field; it is not set
fixed.perturbation: initial position + N(0, 0.5 mm) per axis per rollout; identical arrays for both engines
fixed.pass_gate: finite state, no contact truncation/overflow, and at least one valid rebound apex in every rollout (otherwise the apex term is undefined and the candidate cannot win)
fixed.loss: per trial: trajectory RMSE (m) + 0.05 x E_apex over the first <=3 apexes; mean over trials
fixed.mechanism_metrics: apex-to-apex restitution sequence e_k = sqrt(h_k+1/h_k) vs the real sequence, DTW, contact duration (simulation only)

selection_rule: pass gate, then mean selection loss, then wall time
seed_rule: selection: seed0 + trial index (same for every candidate); held-out cell j, trial i: seed0 + 1000 + 100*j + i

candidate_rule.rationale: both engines span normal stiffness and dissipation (SAP ke/tau, MuJoCo direct k/b); unchanged from dynamic-impact-v1

held_out_conditions.axis: release height (real reference from the apex onward)
release height (real reference from the apex onward)

not_run_conditions.reason: the public drops are vertical with no lateral velocity; no reference exists
